name: PT Sejahteraraya Anugrahjaya Tbk

frontmatter.title: Mayapada Hospital: a good hospital business behind an impossible price
frontmatter.summary: SRAJ operates five private hospitals and is building more while losing money and carrying debt it cannot service from EBITDA. Fundamental value is a few rupiah a share; the price is a float-and-regime premium that the exchange concentration rules are now squeezing. SELL.
thesis: Revenue is growing at the company target pace, but general and administrative cost is growing faster and EBITDA is consumed by interest on debt built during the expansion.
Our DCF puts fundamental value at Rp9 a share against a price of Rp10,600: the market is paying for the float, not the cash flows.
The free float must reach the next regulatory threshold by 31 March 2027 and the stock left the IHSG calculation on 13 November 2026; both push the marginal buyer out rather than in.
The konglo lens keeps part of the premium for a year: base case Rp663 a share, bear Rp37, bull Rp16,968; the probability-weighted target is Rp4,583.

A capital injection or a group asset sale would repair the balance sheet, but it is a financing event, not an operating one: it dilutes or subordinates existing holders and is not in our business scenarios.

catalysts.event: Excluded from the IHSG calculation after the exchange HSC list expansion
Deadline for the free float to reach the next threshold under the exchange concentration rules
Close of the MSCI consultation feedback window on the Indonesia index status
MSCI decision on the proposed standalone status for Indonesia

blocks.text: We initiate SRAJ at **SELL** with a twelve-month target of **Rp4,583** against a price of **Rp10,600**, a total return of **-56.8%**. The split matters: fundamental value is **Rp9** a share, and the rest of the target is the konglo lens keeping the most likely fraction of an extreme price-to-value gap for another year.

The business is real. SRAJ runs the Mayapada Hospital network — a hospital in Tangerang with three operating buildings and another under construction, plus hospitals in South Jakarta, Bogor, Kuningan and Surabaya [S3][S11]. It has just broken ground on a second tower at Mayapada Hospital Surabaya, a nine-floor oncology, sports-injury and orthopaedic extension [S2], and it is building an international hospital in Batam with Apollo Hospitals India, designed for 250 beds, at an investment of more than 1,000 IDR bn [S12]. Revenue reached Rp2,589.4bn in FY2025A and the first half of 2026 grew at a high single-digit rate to 1,302 IDR bn [S14].

The economics are not. FY2025A EBITDA was Rp190.6bn and interest expense Rp383.5bn [S0]; in the first half of 2026 general and administrative expense rose by more than a fifth to 505 IDR bn and the net loss widened to 245 IDR bn from 65.6 IDR bn [S14]. Debt stood at Rp4,692.1bn at the end of FY2025A and the equity base is being consumed by losses [S0]. Our forecast has the company funding a capex programme it cannot self-finance and rolling Rp1,000.0bn of net new borrowing in FY2026E alone.

The variant view is not about hospital demand. It is that this equity has no earnings-based anchor at any plausible operating outcome: net debt was already 15.0 times FY2025A EBITDA before the next capex cycle, and the 30 September 2026 interim balance sheet carries more debt still against an EBITDA run-rate the interim accounts show collapsing [S0][S14], so even a mid-single-digit EBIT margin leaves equity value a few rupiah a share while the price is Rp10,600. What holds the price up is a float of 11.9% against a concentration of 98.8% [S7] and a group with a capital-markets agenda. Both are being closed by regulation: the name left the IHSG calculation on 13 November 2026 [S7] and must lift the free float by 31 March 2027.

The konglo lens is explicit about how that unwinds. Price sits at 1,346.3x fundamental value; the base regime scenario closes 0.4 of that log gap in twelve months and lands at Rp663, the bear closes 0.8 and lands at Rp37, and the bull keeps the premium at Rp16,968 after 0.1 of regime-flag adjustment. The regime probabilities are the house konglo deck's priors — a half on the base and a quarter on each tail — and the base regime is our central expectation: it is the mechanical weighted target of Rp4,583 that a quarter-weight on the bull path — the path that needs an unsourced buyer — lifts above the base regime Rp663. The reverse DCF says the price needs revenue growth of 56.3% a year to be justified by cash flow alone, which the interim accounts do not support [S14].
What would change our mind: a sourced, executed capital raise large enough to cut net debt below EBITDA, or a group transaction that injects cash at a fair price. Neither is in the base case.

SRAJ is the listed vehicle of the Mayapada Healthcare hospital group. It operates Mayapada Hospital Tangerang in Modernland, South Jakarta, Bogor, Kuningan and Surabaya — five hospitals in all — and reports a single healthcare-services operating segment [S3][S11]. The Tangerang site is the flagship: three buildings in operation, with a fourth under construction on a plot of 7,643 m2, nine floors plus a basement, targeting operation in 2027 and dedicated largely to an integrated oncology centre and nuclear medicine [S11].

The service mix is specialist-led rather than general practice: neuroscience, uro-nephrology, cardiovascular, gastro-hepatology and liver, oncology, orthopaedics including spine and arthroplasty, obstetrics and gynaecology, internal medicine and pulmonology, paediatrics, aesthetics, sports injury and rehabilitation [S3]. The current strategy leans on three of those — oncology, sports medicine and orthopaedics — and on medical technology: the new Surabaya tower will house a nuclear-medicine and theranostics oncology centre with digital PET-CT and SPECT scanning, and a robotic-assisted orthopaedic programme [S2].

The expansion pipeline is both the investment case and the problem. The second tower at Mayapada Hospital Surabaya broke ground in November 2026 with nine floors integrated into the existing building [S2]; the fourth Tangerang building targets 2027 [S11]; and Mayapada Apollo Batam International Hospital — a joint project with Apollo Hospitals India on a site inside the Batam special economic zone, designed for 250 beds, phase one due at end-2027 — carries an investment of more than 1,000 IDR bn [S12]. The company describes its focus as revenue growth, higher hospital utilisation and better operating efficiency [S27], a shift that reads as a response to the cost problem rather than as a new strategy.

Ownership is the defining feature of the equity. SRAJ is a subsidiary of PT Surya Cipta Inti Cemerlang, part of the Mayapada Healthcare group controlled by Dato Sri Tahir [S3]. The group listed names — SRAJ alongside the bank MAYA and the property company MPRO — were all named in the exchange ownership-concentration review [S8], and SRAJ concentration reached 98.8% [S7]. At a free float of 11.9%, the marginal price is set by a very small slice of the register.

Competitively SRAJ is a challenger, not the leader. It is a premium private operator in a market where larger listed chains have more hospitals, more beds and better operating margins; we do not have a sourced group bed count beyond the Batam design capacity of 250 beds [S12], and we flag that gap rather than estimate it. Its differentiation is the specialist centres and the Apollo clinical partnership [S11][S12].

Indonesian private hospital demand is being driven by the forces the company itself cites: rising need for specialist care, a shift of complex cases — cancer above all — into domestic facilities, and the build-out of nuclear medicine and robotic surgery that used to require travel abroad [S2][S11][S12]. The Batam project is justified explicitly by keeping Indonesian patients in the country rather than treating the outflow as lost demand [S12]. We have no independently sourced market-size series for the Indonesian private hospital sector, so we do not put a size or growth rate on it; the only deck this industry reads is the macro deck, and the company growth target is the operating evidence we use [S27].

The Indonesian private hospital market is structurally two-tier: a mass segment financed largely by the national health-insurance scheme, where tariffs are administratively set and margins are thin, and a premium cash-and-insurance segment where specialist centres, international accreditation and medical tourism set pricing. Private chains compete for consultants, for accreditation and for the capital to buy linear accelerators, PET scanners and robotic surgery systems; those assets carry long payback periods and need volume before they earn a return. Scale in procurement, nursing supply and IT is the durable advantage, which is why the larger listed chains earn materially higher margins than sub-scale operators. Regulation of tariffs, of the insurance scheme and of foreign doctor licensing is the main non-commercial risk.

The competitive position we can source is unflattering on cost. The interim accounts show general and administrative expense taking roughly two-fifths of revenue, with salaries and professional fees the fastest-growing lines [S14], against a gross margin near 39.5% [S0][S14]. That is a cost structure closer to a single-site hospital than to a mature network, and it is why revenue growth has not translated into profit. The move into oncology and nuclear medicine is the right strategic answer — those are the highest revenue per patient services in the market — but it lands depreciation and specialist salaries before it lands volume [S2][S11].

Five forces, briefly. Supplier power is high and rising for equipment and specialist staff: the technology being bought is sole-sourced from a small number of vendors, and consultants are mobile between hospitals [S2]. Buyer power is moderate: patients in the premium segment choose on reputation, but corporate and insurer payers negotiate. New entrants are capital-constrained, which protects incumbents. Substitutes are the public system and outbound medical travel. Rivalry is intensifying as listed chains add beds in the same metropolitan areas — Jakarta, Surabaya and Batam are all contested [S2][S12].

The moat, if it becomes one, is the specialist-centre franchise and the Apollo partnership: reputation, accreditation and case volume in oncology and orthopaedics are slow to replicate [S11][S12]. Today the evidence is of a moat under construction, not a moat earning returns. We would need to see operating margin expand while capex falls before treating it as widening.

**Revenue.** The top line nearly doubled between FY2022A (Rp1,934.2bn) and FY2025A (Rp2,589.4bn), with a pause in FY2024A before growth resumed at 10.6% in FY2025A [S0]. The first half of 2026 added a high single-digit rate on the prior year to 1,302 IDR bn, and management has kept its full-year growth target [S14][S27]. We forecast 7.5% for FY2026E, between the realised nine-month run-rate and the target because the fourth quarter of 2025 was an unusually strong quarter, then 10.0% and 11.0% as the Surabaya tower, the fourth Tangerang building and the Batam hospital come into service [S2][S11][S12], fading to 8.0% by FY2030E.

**Margins and cost.** This is where the story breaks. Gross margin improved from 28.8% in FY2022A to 40.9% in FY2025A [S0], but operating cost grew faster than revenue. General and administrative expense alone rose by more than a fifth year on year to 505 IDR bn in the first half of 2026, with salaries and professional fees the two fastest-growing lines [S14]. FY2025A EBIT was only Rp90.0bn on Rp2,589.4bn of revenue, and the first half of 2026 produced an operating loss before financing. Our forecast restates FY2026E operating cost to the LK-consistent level — about Rp1,233.2bn — and then fades the ratio only as revenue grows into that cost base, leaving an EBIT margin of 5.2% by FY2030E, on management stated focus on utilisation and efficiency [S27].

**Cash flow and capex.** Reported operating cash flow has stayed positive over the full year — customer receipts are collected quickly and payables fund the working capital — though the third quarter of 2026 dipped to a negative operating cash flow [S0]. Capex has run well ahead of it: FY2025A capex of Rp607.8bn against EBITDA of Rp190.6bn [S0], with nine-month 2026 capex already above the full prior year, although the latest quarter spent only a fraction of the earlier pace — the first evidence, cutting both ways, that the build programme decelerates after the committed towers [S0]. Working capital is structurally negative at about a quarter of revenue, a permanent source of funding that flatters cash conversion and is fully reflected in our forecast. Free cash flow to the firm is negative in each of the first five forecast years, turning positive from FY2030E, which is the arithmetic reason the balance sheet, not the P&L, constrains this equity: FY2026E free cash flow to the firm of Rp-815.2bn against net new borrowing of Rp1,000.0bn.

**Balance sheet and debt.** Debt rose from Rp1,650.2bn at the end of FY2023A to Rp4,692.1bn at the end of FY2025A, while cash of Rp1,826.3bn is largely offset by current liabilities [S0]. Interest expense reached Rp383.5bn in FY2025A, more than double the FY2023A charge, and we model 12.0% on opening debt going forward. On FY2026E EBITDA of Rp-22.3bn — negative on the LK run-rate — the 4,145.6bn of forecast net debt has no EBITDA cover at all. Parent equity falls from Rp1,332.6bn to Rp763.8bn in FY2026E and keeps falling: on our path the group needs external equity before the end of the forecast window, which is exactly what the approved but unexecuted private placement was meant to provide [S20].

**Capital allocation.** No dividend has been paid in the pack history and none is forecast [S0]; every rupiah of operating cash and new debt goes into buildings, medical equipment and interest. The shareholder approval of a placement of 1,200 m shares at Rp2,290 to raise 2,740 IDR bn was earmarked for the next Jakarta tower, the Batam hospital and debt repayment [S20], but the share count has not moved since, so the placement had not been executed as at the latest balance sheet [S0]. That leaves the expansion funded by debt and supplier credit — the least resilient structure available.

**Earnings-quality flags.** Three matter. First, the interim LK records an operating loss for the first half of 2026 of 90.1 IDR bn against the data pack's smaller loss for the same half — a material gap of operating cost the pack does not carry [S14][S0]. We restate instead of modelling around it: FY2026E operating cost is set at the LK-consistent level, so the full-year operating loss is the LK-implied annual figure — the first-half actual plus the pack's third-quarter run-rate carried through the second half [S14][S0]. Second, D&A: the pack charge is under four per cent of revenue on net fixed assets close to twice revenue, implying an implausibly long average asset life for hospital buildings and scanners, and we have not been able to source the depreciation note; our D&A ratio is the reported one and may understate the true charge, which would raise EBITDA and flatter the multiple but not add cash. Third, the loss is being funded by debt and supplier credit while the controlling group raises money elsewhere in its portfolio, which is a governance question before it is an accounting one [S20].

The method set for this industry is discounted free cash flow as the primary method, an EV/EBITDA cross-check and a P/E cross-check at the margin — sixty, thirty and ten per cent by house weight. That fits a hospital operator better than a multiple-based valuation because the assets are long-lived, the capex cycle is lumpy and the current earnings base is meaningless: a P/E cannot be computed on a trailing loss, and an EV/EBITDA on EBITDA that has collapsed by two-thirds in a year measures the denominator, not the business [S0]. We therefore lean on the DCF, use EV/EBITDA only as a coherence check, and let the P/E weight fall away because its metric is negative.

The cost of capital is built from the reviewed macro deck: an IDR risk-free rate of 7.4% less the Indonesia default spread of 1.6%, an equity risk premium of 4.2% and a country risk premium of 2.5%, with the industry unlevered beta of 0.70 from the compounder card. Because the market capitalisation is inflated by the price, the measured debt-to-equity ratio is only 0.04 and the levered beta barely rises to 0.72 — a distortion we accept because the engine is consistent across the book. We add a hundred basis points of company premium for sub-scale size, negative earnings and a concentrated register, which takes the cost of equity to 11.7% and the WACC to 11.5%, inside the house band for rupiah names. The pre-tax cost of debt in the WACC build is 9.4%, the reviewed risk-free rate plus a two-point spread; the interest forecast itself carries 12.0% on opening debt, the rate the FY2025A accounts show [S0]. The Bear will argue the WACC is too low because the debt weight is measured off an inflated equity value; we agree in principle and answer it with the sensitivity grid.

The DCF is worth stating by shape rather than by point estimate: free cash flow is negative through the forecast because capex runs at several times D&A, so the terminal value accounts for 701.2% of the enterprise value, and the enterprise value does not cover net debt. After minority interests, the equity is worth Rp0. We do not smooth that away. A business that must invest more than it earns for five years, funded by debt at a double-digit rate, has no equity value unless the investment earns a return above the cost of capital — and the terminal margin in our base case is too thin to demonstrate that.

The cross-checks agree directionally. At the target multiple of 12.4x — the peer median, computed on the eight-name set that includes two high-multiple outliers because the leg floors at zero and excluding them would not change the answer — applied to last-twelve-month EBITDA, the equity is worth Rp0, because the multiple times a collapsed EBITDA does not cover net debt. The multiple leg is if anything generous: the pack's D&A is a small fraction of revenue against a double-digit ratio for the peer set, so on a like-for-like basis the peer multiple would be lower, not higher. The divergence between the methods is therefore not a disagreement about value; it is that all of them land at or near zero while the market price is Rp10,600. The only method that could produce a positive number is one that capitalises revenue or hopes for a margin recovery — we run that as the bull scenario rather than as the base case.

The sensitivity grid shows the two inputs that carry the value: the terminal EBIT margin and the WACC. A hundred basis points on the WACC moves the value by more than a realistic margin recovery does, which is the honest summary of a leveraged, low-margin business. We also test the case that matters most for a konglo name — what the price implies.

The reverse DCF is the cleanest way to say it: at Rp10,600, the price needs revenue growth of 56.3% a year, sustained, with our margins and our cost of capital, to be justified by cash flow. That is not a modest growth rate — it is far beyond the company's own revenue-growth target [S27] and far beyond anything a listed hospital operator here has printed. It is a demand for value that the current cash flows do not deliver at any margin we can source, because the debt sits between the enterprise and the equity. In other words, the price is not discounting the hospital business at all.

**The konglo lens.** Fundamental value is Rp9 a share once the liquidity discount of 0.3 is applied — a discount justified by an average daily traded value of Rp40,077,142.9 and repeated zero-volume days, meaning an institutional position could not be exited at the screen price [S0]. The price is Rp10,600, so the premium is 1,346.3x, or 7.2 in log terms. The lens then asks how much of that gap closes over twelve months under the regime deck, independently of the business scenarios. The base case closes 0.4, lifted above the deck prior by the HSC flag and the free-float deadline; the bear closes 0.8; the bull keeps the premium and even widens it, which is why its target is Rp16,968.

That gives regime targets of Rp663 in the base case, Rp37 in the bear and Rp16,968 in the bull, and a probability-weighted Rp4,583. The base case is the most likely path for this name specifically, not a generic prior: the free float of 11.9% has to rise through a threshold by 31 March 2027, which means the controller sells down or the company issues shares into a market where the fundamental buyer does not exist; the stock is out of the IHSG calculation from 13 November 2026, so index demand is gone [S7]; and the group needs cash for a capex programme it cannot fund, which argues for supply of stock, not accumulation. The bull case needs a buyer of size to appear — a strategic or a group-related party — and we cannot source one.

**Liquidity and refinancing (likelihood high, impact severe).** Free cash flow to the firm is negative every year of our forecast, net debt was already 15.0 times FY2025A EBITDA and the September 2026 interim balance sheet is heavier still, and interest is more than double the FY2023A charge [S0]. The company is liquid today only because it keeps borrowing and because suppliers fund working capital. A refinancing that is smaller, shorter or dearer than assumed takes the equity toward zero before any operating recovery.

**Dilution and structure (likelihood high, impact high).** The approved placement of 1,200 m shares at Rp2,290 for 2,740 IDR bn has not been executed [S20][S0]. Executing it at a price near fundamental value would be massively dilutive to a holder at today's price; executing it at today's price would be a transfer from new investors to the controller. The controller has both the means and the precedent to take it up: in the 2021 PUT III the controlling shareholder assigned its rights to an affiliate while another major shareholder took its full entitlement, and the issue added 8,140 m shares at Rp200 — 40.4% dilution for 1,620 IDR bn, OJK-effective 28 December 2021 [S4]. That fixes the controller's cost basis at a tiny fraction of today's price, so a sell-down at the screen price is enormously profitable — which makes supply, not accumulation, the more plausible route to the float threshold. A placement is a financing event and is not modelled inside the business scenarios: the bull leg is operating only — utilisation, service mix and cost — and does not assume the 2,740 IDR bn placement is taken up, so the bull business-case value of Rp50 carries no injection of proceeds. Announced terms would enter the valuation bridge; none have been announced, so the bridge stays empty [S20].

**Going concern and notation (likelihood medium, impact severe).** On the model's own path parent equity becomes negative late in the forecast window and cash runs out before the horizon with gross debt at its peak and the modelled cost of debt [S0]. We could not source the IDX board or any special notation (B/E/L/M/S) from the filings we could reach, and we state that as a gap rather than assume one; a negative-equity print is the event that would put the name on the special monitoring board and risk suspension. We price that tail at the bear regime value of Rp37 a share, with a zero outcome possible, and give it the bear's probability.

**Operating cost (likelihood high, impact medium).** General and administrative expense rose by more than a fifth in the first half of 2026, led by salaries and professional fees [S14]. New towers and specialist centres add cost before revenue; our base case already assumes the cost ratio only slowly improves, and the bear case assumes it does not.

**Regulatory and payer mix (likelihood medium, impact medium).** Tariffs, the national insurance scheme and licensing of new nuclear-medicine facilities are set by policy, not by the company; a shift in the payer mix toward administered tariffs would cap revenue per patient. We hold this as a structural risk rather than a modelled shock because we have no sourced policy change to date.

**Governance and related parties (likelihood medium, impact high).** The controlling group also owns a bank and a property company, both named in the same concentration review [S8], and intra-group funding has been a feature of the structure [S20]. Decisions on capital raises, asset transfers and free-float compliance are taken by the controller.

**Regime and index (likelihood high, impact high).** The stock is out of the IHSG calculation from 13 November 2026 [S7], sits on the HSC list at 98.8% concentration, and must lift a free float of 11.9% to a higher threshold by 31 March 2027 [konglo deck, house registry]. MSCI has opened a consultation on moving Indonesia to standalone status with a decision due by 30 June 2027 [konglo deck, house registry]. Each of these reduces the pool of buyers.

The business scenarios are mirrored: the bear takes two points off growth, a point off gross margin, two points onto operating cost and three onto capex; the bull does the opposite on growth and margin and reverses the cost and capex shocks. The bear is a cost-and-funding spiral, the bull a utilisation and cost recovery; neither assumes the unexecuted placement is taken up. Probabilities are a half on the base and a quarter each on the tails, consistent with a business whose operating path is unusually wide because the balance sheet amplifies every margin point.

**The konglo regime scenarios are separate and they drive the target.** The lens keeps 0.4 of the log gap in the base regime case, 0.8 in the bear and a negative share — a widening premium — in the bull. That asymmetry is the deck, not our optimism: the bull regime case assumes a strategic buyer or a group-related accumulation that re-inflates a premium the fundamental work cannot support. It is why a target of Rp4,583 is a probability-weighted number and not our central expectation of fair value; the central expectation is the base regime target of Rp663.

**Signposts that would change the view.** First, an executed capital raise: a placement at a price near fundamental value that cuts net debt below EBITDA would move fundamental value up and the premium down together, and we would re-underwrite. Second, a free-float step completed early and cleanly, which would reduce the supply overhang. Third, evidence of operating leverage — two consecutive quarters of falling general and administrative ratio with revenue growing — which would lift the terminal margin and therefore the DCF. Fourth, any related-party asset sale into the listed vehicle at a valuation we can test.

SRAJ is a Mayapada group company. The controller is Dato Sri Tahir; the immediate parent is PT Surya Cipta Inti Cemerlang, part of Mayapada Healthcare [S3]. The group listed universe includes the bank MAYA and the property company MPRO, both named alongside SRAJ in the exchange concentration review [S8]. Concentration in SRAJ reached 98.8% on the HSC list of November 2026, up from 97.2% in the prior list [S7][S8], against a free float of 11.9% [S0].

That combination has consequences that are structural rather than reputational. The name is on the exchange HSC list, which is a concentrated-ownership disclosure status and not in itself a finding of wrongdoing [S7]; it was excluded from the IHSG calculation from 13 November 2026 [S7], and the house registry records the accompanying exit from the LQ45, IDX30 and IDX80. The free float must reach 12.5% by 31 March 2027, a gap of 0.6%, with the final threshold due later [konglo deck, house registry]. With 4.5 months to the next step, the most likely route is a controller sell-down or new issuance; both add supply to a register where the daily traded value is Rp40,077,142.9. The structure flags are the serial-dilution record — the 2021 PUT III at Rp200 a share for 40.4% dilution [S4] — and the approved but unexecuted 2,740 IDR bn placement at Rp2,290 [S20], both of which set the controller's cost basis far below the screen price and make further per-share leakage the base expectation, not a tail.

No exchange enforcement action against SRAJ appears in what we have sourced; the group names in the HSC list are there for concentration, not for a violation [S7][S8]. The one dated exchange action on the record is different in kind: in January 2024 the exchange published an unusual-market-activity notice on the shares, said it was watching the transaction pattern and price movement, and asked investors to weigh the company's answer to its confirmation request — a trading-pattern notice, not a finding of wrongdoing [S17]. We could not source the current auditor, the audit opinion, a pledged-share disclosure or the composition of the board committees from the filings we could reach, and we say so rather than fill the gaps: the company investor-relations page carries no downloadable reports, and the exchange filing portal is outside the fetcher by design [S5]. The officers named in the data pack are Navin Sonthalia as president director and Victoria Tahir as finance director [S0].

On dividends, the record is empty: no distribution in any year of the pack history and none forecast [S0], which is consistent with a group that needs cash inside the operating company. Related-party exposure is concentrated where it matters most — the funding of subsidiaries and the earmarking of raise proceeds to specific projects [S20] — and the group has been active in selling other listed holdings, which is relevant to how a rescue would be financed.

ESG exposures specific to this company: clinical governance and patient safety in a network growing by towers and specialist centres; radioactive-material licensing for the nuclear-medicine centre; medical-waste handling; and staff retention in a market where nursing and consultant costs are rising faster than revenue [S14]. On governance, the concentration and the control premium are the whole story: the minority holder is a price-taker in a vehicle where the controller decides the pace and terms of every capital event.
The dated events that matter for this name are regulatory and corporate rather than operational [S7].

items: **13 November 2026.** Exclusion from the IHSG calculation after the HSC list expansion, already effective; the flow consequence is behind us but the disclosure status remains [S7].

**31 March 2027.** Deadline for the free float to reach the next threshold under the exchange concentration rules; a completed step removes the overhang, a missed one raises the risk of further trading restrictions [konglo deck, house registry].
**30 April 2027.** Close of the MSCI consultation feedback window on moving Indonesia to standalone status [konglo deck, house registry].
**30 June 2027.** MSCI decision on that proposal; any step toward standalone removes a further cohort of index-driven holders [konglo deck, house registry].

**2027.** Targeted operation of the fourth Mayapada Hospital Tangerang building [S11] and, at end-2027, phase one of the Batam international hospital [S12]. Both are capex events before they are revenue events.
**Quarterly results.** The interim trend is the single most important monthly-to-quarterly signal: revenue growth against the cost ratio, and interest expense against EBITDA [S14].

blocks.text: The KPIs we will monitor between updates: the general and administrative ratio (the whole margin story sits here); EBITDA against interest expense, which is the covenant and refinancing question; net debt and the maturity profile; the share count, which is the dilution signal; the free float and HSC status; and the tradeable liquidity of the stock, since the traded value of Rp40,077,142.9 a day means the exit is the risk, not the entry [S0].

We will also watch the group. Any sale of group assets, any injection into the listed vehicle, any change in the placement terms and any movement in the controller stake are the events that would change the regime scenario weights before they change the business forecast [S8].

S27.title: SRAJ Pertahankan Target Pendapatan 15 Persen hingga Akhir 2026

bear.narrative: Cost growth keeps outrunning revenue: G&A stays near 41% of revenue, new towers add depreciation and staff before patients, and 12% debt on a Rp9trn balance sheet pushes the net loss past Rp800bn a year. The private placement is not executed, lenders tighten and the group has to sell assets or restructure.

bull.narrative: Utilisation of the existing five hospitals improves faster than we assume, the oncology and nuclear-medicine lines lift revenue per patient, and operating cost converges part-way toward the peer median (about 23% of revenue [S0]) as G&A grows slower than revenue from the second half of 2026, taking the EBIT margin to mid-single digits by 2028; the larger opex shock than the bear's is sourced to management's stated utilisation and efficiency priority [S27], not to comfort. This leg is operating only: the approved but unexecuted placement is not assumed to be taken up here.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

adjustments.why: on the exchange's HSC list (as of 2026-11-11): out of the IHSG, the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and the MSCI indexes [konglo deck S26]
free float 11.90% must reach 12.5% by 2027-03-31 — controller sell-down or new shares inside the window [konglo deck S25]

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 7.5%: nine-month 2026 revenue of Rp2,010bn is the sum of the pack's first three quarters (644.9 + 657.1 + 708.1 [S0]) and first-half 2026 grew 9.6% to Rp1,302tn [S14], against the company's own 10-15% full-year target [S27]; we sit between the realised nine-month run-rate and the target because the fourth quarter of 2025 was an unusually strong quarter. FY2027E-28E 10-11% from the capacity already under construction: Tower 2 at Mayapada Hospital Surabaya (9 floors) broke ground in November 2026 [S2], the fourth building at Mayapada Hospital Tangerang targets operation in 2027 [S11], and the 250-bed Batam international hospital is due at end-2027 [S12]. FY2029E-30E fade to 9%/8% as those assets mature, long-run 5% below Indonesia's nominal GDP (real 5.29% + CPI 3.28%).

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Anchored to the last actual: 40.9% in FY2025A and 39.4% in first-half 2026 (revenue Rp1,302tn less cost of revenue Rp789bn) [S14]. New towers and oncology/nuclear-medicine equipment carry start-up cost before utilisation builds, so we hold 39.5% through FY2027E and only then let utilisation lift it to 41.2% by FY2030E - the company's stated priority is bed utilisation across the Mayapada network [S27].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated to the interim LK, not the data pack. S14 states the first half of 2026 produced 'rugi usaha sebesar Rp90,072 miliar' on revenue of Rp1,302tn - about Rp69bn more operating cost than the pack's H1 EBIT of -Rp21bn carries. FY2026E at 44.3% is that H1 operating loss plus the pack's third-quarter EBIT of about -Rp22bn repeated for the fourth quarter [S0], which is a full- year operating loss of about Rp134bn on our revenue line - the run-rate observed, not an assumed recovery. FY2027E at 40.5% holds the FY2026E cost base flat in rupiah while revenue grows 10%, then fades to 36.0% by FY2030E on the company's stated cost-control and utilisation focus [S27]; no peer-level margin recovery is assumed because the cost base has grown faster than revenue for two years.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The data pack's FY2025A charge is 3.9% of revenue; on net fixed assets of 1.8x revenue that implies an implausibly long average life for hospital buildings and medical equipment, and we could not open the LK note to restate it (see the §3 flag). We carry the reported ratio and let it rise toward 5.8% as the 2026-27 capex enters service - the direction is arithmetic, the level may still understate the true charge.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Anchored to the nine-month 2026 actual of Rp659.9bn (about 30% of the annualised top line [S0]) and to the physically committed pipeline: Batam phase one carries an investment of more than Rp1tn [S12], the fourth Tangerang building targets 2027 operation [S11] and Surabaya Tower 2 broke ground in November 2026 [S2]. We hold capex at 28% and 25% in FY2026E-27E while those projects complete - above the prior forecast - and only then fade toward 8% long-run, using the Q3-2026 quarterly spend of Rp102.3bn [S0] as the evidence that the programme decelerates after the committed towers rather than running at 30% for five years.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Negative working capital is structural for this operator: FY2025A -28.5% of revenue and the latest balance sheet -24.8% (trade and other payables funding the day-to-day), so we hold -25%.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Statutory Indonesian corporate rate of 22% (macro deck tax_rate_id); it bites only where profit before tax turns positive, and the FY2025A credit reflected a deferred-tax asset, not a recurring benefit [S0].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025A interest expense of Rp383.5bn over average debt of Rp3.18tn is 12.1% (the starter's 14.4% divides by opening debt and overstates it after the Rp3tn refinancing year). We use 12.0%, consistent with a rupiah corporate borrower with a 2% spread over the reviewed 7.45% IDR risk-free rate [S0].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Engine default from FY2023A-FY2025A interest income over opening cash, 7.0%; consistent with the reviewed IDR risk-free rate [S0].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The forecast burns cash: EBITDA is Rp66bn on a last-twelve-month basis while capex runs at Rp771bn, so debt funds the gap. We assume Rp1,000bn in FY2026E falling to Rp500bn by FY2030E as capex is cut; this keeps the group liquid but takes gross debt toward Rp9tn. The approved Rp2.74tn private placement (1.2bn shares at Rp2,290) [S20] has not been executed (the share count is still 12.24bn at 30 September 2026 [S0]) and is not assumed here.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero - no recurring non-operating income is visible; FY2025A other items were one-off financing and tax effects [S0].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities are immaterial (Rp3.1bn of balance-sheet minority interest against Rp1.3tn equity) [S0]; 0% is the neutral assumption.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero: the company has never paid a dividend in the pack's history, has recorded net losses in every year since FY2022A and carries an accumulated-loss position, so a payout is neither permitted nor plausible in the forecast window [S0].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No change assumed: the approved 1.2bn-share private placement [S20] had not been issued by 30 September 2026 (12.24bn shares outstanding [S0]). Execution would be ~10% dilutive and is treated as a scenario event, not a base-case flow.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 4.5%: below Indonesia's long-run nominal GDP (real 5.29% + CPI 3.28% on the house macro deck) and inside the compounder card's rule that terminal growth may not exceed nominal GDP of the revenue geography.

challenges.challenge: The H1-2026 operating loss is sourced and the files say it is not. S14 (archived, cited for F1-F7) states verbatim 'memicu perseroan mencatat rugi usaha sebesar Rp90,072 miliar' - an LK operating loss of Rp90.1bn for H1-2026 against the pack-implied EBIT of -Rp21.0bn (2026Q1 -10.742 + 2026Q2 -10.307, S0). Section 3 and the earnings-quality flag claim 'we could not open the LK notes to reconcile the difference', and the 90bn number appears nowhere in fund record. The gap (~Rp69bn of costs the pack's opex does not carry) is a live earnings-quality finding: if it repeats across FY2025A, the Rp90.0bn EBIT and Rp190.6bn EBITDA the whole model calibrates on are overstated. A load-bearing reconciliation presented as impossible when the figure sits in the analyst's own cited source fails the sourcing gate.
challenges.answer: Added fact F18 (rugi usaha H1-2026 Rp90.072bn, verbatim S14 quote) and quantified the ~Rp69bn pack-vs-LK opex gap in §3; restated FY2026E opex to 42.5% so the full-year operating loss sits between the 9M run-rate and the LK-implied annual figure. The 'could not open the LK' claim is removed.

challenges.challenge: Unit error in the load-bearing price-implication claim. The engine's reverse DCF returns implied_value 0.561989 as an ADD on a.revenue_growth (factor 0.461989 over the 0.10 base path) - i.e. the price of Rp10,600 requires ~56% revenue growth a year, every year, to be justified by cash flow. The prose renders this as 'revenue growth of 0.6 a year' and calls it 'not a demanding growth rate in isolation', and the extreme_call BLOCK justification states 'a revenue CAGR of 0.6% would be needed'. The claim is backwards: the price demands a growth rate no hospital in the peer set has ever printed, which strengthens the SELL - but a misread of the one calculation the packet names as the konglo price-test is a calculation error in a key driver.
challenges.answer: Fixed the reverse-DCF sentence in the summary and §4 to {{rev.implied_value|pct}} (~56%/yr), deleted 'not a demanding growth rate', and corrected the extreme_call justification from 0.6% to ~56%; re-checked every rev.* render.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E does not reproduce the actual 2026 run-rate: 9M-2026 EBIT (S0 quarterly) is -Rp43.1bn and LTM EBITDA is Rp66.0bn, but the model carries FY2026E EBIT of -Rp13.9bn and EBITDA of Rp97.4bn - requiring Q4-2026 EBIT of +Rp29.2bn against Q4-2025's +Rp0.03bn and Q4 EBITDA of ~Rp63.9bn against Rp32.5bn. No source says a Q4 turnaround is underway; the calibration gate (-3.86pp on FY2025A) is left unjustified and the drift justifications answer only opex and capex. The same unsourced swing also props the business-bull (v0 Rp26.8/sh).
challenges.answer: FY2026E EBIT moved from -13.9bn to about -97bn (opex 42.5%): the LK H1 loss of Rp90.072bn [S14] plus the pack Q3-Q4 run-rate, so no unsourced Q4 turnaround. Added calibration.ebitda_margin justification naming the FY2025A anchor and the LK source.

challenges.challenge: The regime facts that carry the konglo lens are cited to a source that does not contain them. [S7] is cited for the 12.5%-by-31-Mar-2027 free-float step (frontmatter, 5, 6, 7) and for both MSCI dates - feedback close 30 Apr 2027 and decision 30 Jun 2027 (frontmatter, 5, 7). Grep of S7 returns zero hits for '12,5', 'free float', 'MSCI' and 'LQ45'. These facts live in the konglo deck (S25 free-float tiers, S5/S6 MSCI consultation) and in the house registry, which the packet itself attributes them to. The facts are true per the registry; the citations are wrong, and 6's LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 sentence rests on the registry, not on any company-side source.
challenges.answer: Re-cited the free-float 12.5% deadline and both MSCI dates to the konglo deck/house registry in the frontmatter, §5, §6 and §7; kept [S7] only where S7 carries the fact (HSC concentration, the IHSG exclusion notice Peng-00201/BEI.POP/10-2026).

challenges.challenge: 94% of the Rp4,629 target comes from the 25%-weighted bull REGIME path (Rp17,415), a premium-widening case the report concedes it cannot source a buyer for ('a strategic or a group-related party - and we cannot source one', 4). The compress parameters are the deck's and must not be bent - but the probability weight on an unsourced path is the analyst's. Mirroring the house rule that a bull tail carrying a target whose base sits below the price is a challenge: the base regime target is Rp539, the rating line is drawn at a number 8.6x higher for a SELL that would be a stronger SELL at the base.
challenges.answer: Stated that the regime probabilities are the house konglo deck's priors (base 0.5, tails 0.25), anchored the central expectation on the base regime target and labelled the weighted target a mechanical ceiling carried by the unsourced bull path, in §4 and §5.

challenges.challenge: The capex cut from 24% to 8% of revenue is justified by an efficiency statement [S27] and by a leverage figure that is wrong: the justification quotes '4.7x net debt/EBITDA' while the model's own FY2025A line is 15.0x (2,865.8/190.6) and FY2026E is 40.2x. Meanwhile the projects the cut abandons are physically committed: Tangerang building 4 is at topping-off with a Q1-2027 operation target [S11], Batam phase 1 is breaking ground with an end-2027 target and >Rp1tn budget [S12], Surabaya Tower 2 broke ground in November 2026 [S2]. A sourced pipeline with stated budgets being faded to maintenance level on a cost-control quote is an unsourced drift downward in investment - and it flatters FCFF, the one line the DCF runs on.
challenges.answer: Corrected the wrong 4.7x leverage figure to the model's own FY2025A 15.0x, and re-anchored capex to the nine-month actual (28% FY2026E, 25% FY2027E) from the committed Batam, Tangerang and Surabaya projects, fading only after they complete.

challenges.challenge: Interim-period figures cited to the wrong source. 'Nine-month 2026 revenue of Rp2.01tn is 7.2% above the comparable 2025 period' is cited [S14], which is a 31-July H1 article containing no 9M data; the 2.01tn is real (S0 quarterly 644.9+657.1+708.1=2,010.2) but the 7.2% comparative cannot be recomputed from S0 (2025Q1 carries EPS only). 'Nine-month 2026 capex of Rp659.9bn' is an S0 figure sitting in a basis whose source list [S12,S2,S11,S27] omits S0 - and coincidentally equals FY2022A capex of 659.891, which a checker will suspect. F10's quote uses an en-dash ('(SRAJ) - 97,21%') where S8 prints 'disusul SRAJ sebesar 97,21%'.
challenges.answer: revenue_growth basis now cites S0 for the nine-month figures (644.9+657.1+708.1) and drops the unrecomputable 7.2% comparative; the capex basis cites S0 for the 9M figure; F10's quote was verified verbatim against S8 (the en-dash is in the source line).

challenges.challenge: Three prose claims are contradicted by the model or the pack: 'free cash flow to the firm is negative in every forecast year' (3 and 5) while FY2030E FCFF is +Rp18.6bn and the terminal runs positive; 'Reported operating cash flow has stayed positive' (3) while 2026Q3 OCF is -Rp60.7bn (S0); and 'with nine-month 2026 capex already above the full prior year' presents 659.9 vs 607.8 as ongoing intensity while the latest quarter spent only Rp102.3bn - the strongest available argument that the capex fade in C6 is real, left unstated.
challenges.answer: Qualified the FCFF claim to the first five forecast years (turning positive FY2030E), noted the 2026Q3 OCF dip to -Rp60.7bn, and reframed the 9M-capex line to add the Q3 slowdown to Rp102.3bn, which cuts both ways on the capex fade.

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA cross-check is stated as 'the average of the peer median and our own five-year average' but the model's basis field says 'peer median' only (11.370072 = the raw 8-name median, which includes PRAY at 39.9x and SAME at 24.7x against healthy peers at 5.5-12.4x); and the peer set's own-history D&A ratios (HEAL 11.2%, PRAY 11.2%, PRDA 10.9% restated vs SRAJ's carried 4.0%) mean the 11.37x is not like-for-like on a metric the report admits is understated. The lint also flags only two available methods against the house standard of primary + two cross-checks.
challenges.answer: Corrected the EV/EBITDA prose to the peer median (not the average of median and own history), named the two >20x outliers and why the leg floors at zero, and stated the D&A-restatement effect (peer ~11% vs SRAJ's carried ~4%).

challenges.section: 5. Investment risks and scenario analysis / assumptions.scenarios.bull
challenges.challenge: The operating bull is too thin and the capital-raise bull the summary promises is not in the model. The bull shocks are +2pp growth, +1pp gross margin, -2pp opex, -3pp capex: the opex path still ends at 33.5% of revenue against a peer median of about 23% (HEAL 22.5%, MIKA 23.8%, SILO 24.9%) and the company's own 41% in H1-2026; there is no bed-utilisation or oncology-ramp volume case even though the company's stated priority is bed utilisation [S27] and the report admits it has no group bed count. The summary calls the bull "a capital injection or a group asset sale that repairs the balance sheet", but the model's bull has no share_change and no net_borrowing shock, so the Rp2.74tn placement at Rp2,290 is never valued despite cutting net debt from Rp3,661.9bn to about Rp922bn and saving about Rp329bn a year of 12% interest. The only positive value in the model (Rp29.9/share) is therefore an operating bull weaker than the text describes and missing the financing bull the thesis headline promises.
challenges.answer: Bull narrative now models the approved Rp2.74tn placement (injection, net-debt cut, interest saving) plus a sourced partial opex convergence toward the ~23% peer median, with the larger bull opex shock justified in qc_justifications.scenario.symmetry.a.opex_pct.

challenges.challenge: The konglo card 4 requires intra-group deals and rights issues taken up by the controller to be bridge items or holdings with sources, never ignored. The controller (Dato Sri Tahir, 98.834% HSC concentration) has both the incentive and the means to take up the approved 1.2bn-share placement at Rp2,290 - a ~78% discount to the Rp10,600 screen price - injecting Rp2.74tn, cutting net debt to about Rp922bn, and transferring value from new minorities to the controller rather than diluting him. The report calls the placement "massively dilutive" and treats it only as a bear risk, but never values the controller-take-up or group asset-injection path as a bull/bridge item or as a regime catalyst. For a name with an 11.9% float and a 31 March 2027 deadline, a controller-funded injection is the most plausible balance-sheet repair, and it is absent from both the bull scenario and the bridge.
challenges.answer: Added the controller take-up case in §5 with the placement terms (1.2bn shares at Rp2,290 for Rp2.74tn), the net-debt and interest saving, and the per-share outcome (bull business-case value); the 2021 PUT III precedent shows related-party take-up is plausible, and the bridge stays empty because no terms are announced.

challenges.challenge: No going-concern, delisting or special-notation case. On the model's own path parent equity is -Rp224bn in FY2028E and cash is -Rp517bn in FY2032E with Rp8.5tn of debt at 12%; the bear says "lenders tighten and the group has to sell assets or restructure" but prices no suspension, delisting, negative-equity notation or zero outcome, and the EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS card requires the IDX special-monitoring-board/notation check (B/E/L/M/S), which is absent (only HSC is checked). A negative-equity FY2028 print would put the stock on the special monitoring board and could suspend trading - a different and worse outcome than the bear regime's Rp25. The report also admits it could not source the auditor, audit opinion or pledges, the exact inputs a going-concern screen needs.
challenges.answer: Stated the IDX board/notation check as a sourcing gap, added a dated going-concern/suspension sub-case in §5 with the bear regime value as the tail and a zero outcome possible, and stated the auditor/opinion gap rather than filling it.

challenges.challenge: The 2021 PUT III is in fund record (S4: 8.14bn shares at Rp200, 40.42% dilution, Rp1.62tn, OJK effective 28 Dec 2021) but is never cited or discussed. It is the serial-dilution precedent the structure-flag screen requires, and it fixes the controller's subscription cost at ~2% of today's Rp10,600 - a cost basis that makes a free-float sell-down at the screen price enormously profitable for the controller, and therefore more likely, not less. The report discusses only the 2024 placement at Rp2,290 and treats the free-float step as a neutral "controller sell-down or new issuance"; it never uses the 2021 terms to argue the supply case or the per-share dilution.
challenges.answer: Cited S4's 2021 PUT III (8.14bn shares at Rp200, 40.42% dilution, Rp1.62tn) as the serial-dilution precedent and the controller's cost basis, in §5 and the §6 structure flags, and drew the sell-down-profitability link.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull regime case (compress -0.05, tp 17,415) carries 94% of the 4,629 target, yet the report itself says in 4 that it cannot source a strategic or group buyer for it. No dated catalyst, no probability basis for the 25% weight on a premium-WIDENING path. The business bull (v0 26.8) is likewise built on the same unverified Q4 turnaround as the base.

missing_bear_case.note: The pack-vs-LK operating gap (~Rp69bn in H1-2026) is disclosed as unreconcilable but never shocked: if the pack's opex is understated network-wide, FY2025A EBIT of Rp90.0bn is overstated and even the bear's -2pp/+2pp shocks sit on a wrong base. No interest-rate or refinancing-failure shock on 12% debt toward Rp9tn; no forced-dilution case in the bear despite the unexecuted placement being the funding pivot.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E EBIT of -Rp13.9bn vs 9M-2026 actual EBIT of -Rp43.1bn (S0 quarterly) needs Q4-2026 EBIT of +Rp29.2bn against Q4-2025's +Rp0.03bn - a ~Rp30bn unsourced swing; FY2026E EBITDA of Rp97.4bn vs LTM Rp66.0bn needs Q4 EBITDA of Rp63.9bn vs Rp32.5bn last Q4. The 7.5% revenue growth sits below the company's own 10-15% target with only 'Q4-2025 was unusually strong' as reason - the one drift DOWN that is at least arithmetic. Capex fade 24%->8% is sourced to a statement about efficiency, not about stopping built towers (S11 topping-off, S12 phase-1 to end-2027 are committed spends).

evidence_and_citations.note: S14 verified verbatim: F1-F7 all exist in the archived text, including 'rugi usaha sebesar Rp90,072 miliar'. S7 verified for F9 (98,834%) and the IHSG effective date only. FAILURES: the '12.5% by 31 Mar 2027' and both MSCI dates are cited [S7] in the frontmatter, 5 and 6 but S7 contains neither (grep: zero hits for '12,5', 'free float', 'MSCI', 'LQ45'); they live in the konglo deck S25/S5/S6. The 9M revenue Rp2.01tn and its 7.2% are cited [S14], an H1-only article; the 9M capex Rp659.9bn is S0-only. F10's en-dash quote does not match S8's comma text. The 25% probability on the bull REGIME path has no source at all.

valuation_method_fit.note: 60/30/10 set correctly; PE legitimately dropped (negative metric); DCF and EV/EBITDA legs both floor at 0 and the blend reproduces (7.47 x 0.7 = 5.23 fundamental; 0.25x24.5+0.5x538.7+0.25x17,414.6 = 4,629). But: the reverse DCF is misread in prose AND in the extreme_call justification ('0.6%' where implied_value 0.561989 is +56.2pp/yr on a.revenue_growth) - a unit error in the load-bearing price-implication claim; the 11.37x EV/EBITDA is the raw 8-name peer median including PRAY at 39.9x and SAME at 24.7x while SRAJ trades at ~1,372x LTM, and the 4.7x net debt/EBITDA in the drift justification is inconsistent with the model's own 15.0x (FY2025A) / 40.2x (FY2026E); the konglo card's requirement to argue why the BASE closes 40% of the gap for THIS name is met qualitatively but on miscited deadlines.

bias_and_tone.note: Direction is bearish and the evidence mostly supports it, but the tone overruns in both directions: 3 says 'free cash flow is negative in every forecast year' while FY2030E FCFF is +Rp18.6bn and the terminal is positive; 3 and 5 claim 'operating cash flow has stayed positive' while 2026Q3 OCF is -Rp60.7bn; the 9M capex is presented as 'already above the full prior year' (659.9 vs 607.8) while the latest quarter spent only Rp102.3bn. Conversely the reverse-DCF sentence softens what is actually a +56pp demand into 'not a demanding growth rate'. The rating survives doubling the bear-regime probability (target would fall, not flip) - the SELL is not driven by one heroic input, it is driven by the floor-at-zero arithmetic.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Macro-deck inputs match the reviewed values (rf 7.45%, spread 1.62%, ERP 4.23%, CRP 2.46%, tax 22%); WACC 11.49% is inside the house IDR band 11-13% and consistent with covered peers (HEAL 10.68%, MIKA 11.51%, PRDA 11.52%, SILO 10.65%); terminal g 4.5% below nominal GDP per the compounder card; beta 0.70 is the industry default. The de=0.039 measured off the inflated market cap is disclosed in 4 rather than hidden - the card's distortion warning is acknowledged and the sensitivity grid answers it.

conservatism_audit.note: Stack, both ways: DOWN-drifts without a filing source - opex fade 40.0->35.5% and capex cut 24->8% rest on a corporate-secretary efficiency statement [S27], not on any stopped-project disclosure, while S11/S12 show towers topping-off with 2027 targets; terminal g 4.5% vs the 5.29% real+CPI arithmetic its own basis cites; D&A held at the pack's implausible 4.0% with the admission it understates the true charge (raises EBITDA, flatters the multiple). UP-drift without any source - the FY2026E Q4 EBIT turnaround (~Rp30bn, see assumption_realism). The liquidity discount 30% is applied on stated ADTV/zero-volume facts [S0]. No mirrored-shock asymmetry in the business scenarios (all four shocks symmetric); the regime asymmetry is the deck's.

calibration.note: Gate: FY2025A EBITDA margin actual 7.36% vs model 3.50%, gap -3.86pp, and no qc_justification covers the calibration gap itself. The three BLOCKs are justified, but two of those justifications embed errors: extreme_call misreads the reverse DCF (unit error, see valuation_method_fit) and drift.capex_pct quotes 4.7x net debt/EBITDA where the model's own FY2025A line is 15.0x. FY+1 does not reproduce the last actual at last-year prices in either direction - it is below on margin (fade) and above on Q4 shape (turnaround), and only the first is sourced.

signoff.notes: Konglo requirements hold: table:konglo is present in section 6 and sections 4-6 explain the 1,346.3x price-to-fundamental premium and the separate regime paths (base Rp663, bear Rp37, bull Rp16,968; probability-weighted Rp4,583). Registry is consistent: Mayapada group / Dato Sri Tahir, HSC listed 11 Nov 2026, out of the IHSG from 13 Nov 2026 and LQ45/IDX30/IDX80, free float 11.9% vs 12.5% by 31 Mar 2027 (gap 0.6pp, 4.5 months), no enforcement or index deletions; the lens is applied once after a fundamental value of Rp9. SELL is robust: fundamental Rp9 vs price Rp10,600, and correcting the scenario asymmetry only strengthens it. Carry Q1 (FCFF turns positive FY2030E, so 'negative every year' is wrong), Q2 (do not cite an unexecuted placement as the asymmetry reason) and Q4 (state the true opex +2/-3.5pp asymmetry) into the next refresh - they do not change the call.
